response: Yes, lower fasting plasma glucose levels at diagnosis of type 2 diabetes are associated with improved outcomes. People presenting with type 2 diabetes who have lower initial glycemia, which may indicate an earlier stage of the disease, tend to have fewer adverse clinical outcomes despite similar glycemic progression. This suggests that early detection and intervention may be beneficial in managing the disease and improving patient outcomes. However, since most individuals with type 2 diabetes are asymptomatic at diagnosis, active case detection programs would be required to identify them and provide timely treatment.
